item.title: Rangers hope to stay in playoff hunt in series finale vs. Rays
item.description: The Texas Rangers are beginning to see their playoff hopes drift away.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: The Texas Rangers are beginning to see their playoff hopes drift away. They'll try to start reeling them back in when they host the Tampa Bay Rays in the finale of their four-game series on Sunday afternoon in Arlington, Texas. The Rangers (70-73) have lost two in a row and three of four since pulling within a half game of the final wild-card spot in the American League. Texas will head into Sunday two games back of the Cleveland Guardians and Toronto Blue Jays for the final wild-card berth and three games back of the Houston Astros atop the AL West. "We're going to do whatever we can to try and get this right because time's running out here," Rangers manager Skip Schumaker said following a 6-3, 10-inning loss to the Rays on Saturday. "We've got to start collecting some wins because we're digging ourselves a little bit of a hole right now." The Rangers identified Junior Caminero and Jonathan Aranda as players to stop heading into the series, but they've come up short the past two games. Caminero is 4-for-10 with a double, home run and three RBIs, and Aranda is 4-for-9 with two home runs and five RBIs. "Caminero and Aranda have done some damage against us and we've got to make sure they're not beating us," Schumaker said. "We've got to take a look at exactly what we're doing wrong because they've been slugging and doing damage in the wrong time of the game." Aranda has four home runs overall in the past 11 games after hitting just one in the first 34 games following the All-Star break. "The home runs will come," Aranda said through an interpreter after hitting a three-run homer in the 10th inning of Saturday's win. "I'll take them whenever they do, but I'm a contact hitter first and foremost. So, just being able to feel myself in the box, feeling comfortable and being able to put the ball in play, is the big thing." The Rays (85-57) will try to find some run support for Ian Seymour when he takes the mound on Sunday. Seymour (9-6, 4.21 ERA) has lost his past three starts, but didn't pitch poorly in any of them as the offense scored just two runs while he was in those games. He most recently allowed three runs over 6 1/3 innings in a 3-2 loss to the New York Mets on Monday, going without walking a batter for the second straight outing, and striking out 10. Seymour has faced the Rangers just once in his career. He threw 4 2/3 innings of scoreless relief on July 29 to earn the win in the 3-0 victory. He won his next two outings as well, both starts, before beginning his current winless streak. MacKenzie Gore is penciled in to start for the Rangers on Sunday. Gore (8-10, 4.31) beat the Athletics his last time out. The left-hander held them to one run and five hits in 5 1/3 innings of the 8-5 win. Gore made his only career appearance against the Rays in that July 29 matchup, going seven innings as the starter and taking the loss after allowing all three runs. He allowed first inning home runs to Yandy Diaz and Ryan Vilade. -Field Level Media

item.title: El presidente Infantino se presentará a la reelección en marzo: FIFA
item.description: El presidente de la FIFA, Gianni Infantino, sigue decidido a presentarse a la reelección a pesar de la renovada oposición a su candidatura tras un plan fallido para vender una participación en las competiciones de la FIFA a inversionistas privados, según declaró el domingo un portavoz del organismo mundial del fútbol.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: El presidente de la FIFA, Gianni Infantino, sigue decidido a presentarse a la reelección a pesar de la renovada oposición a su candidatura tras un plan fallido para vender una participación en las competiciones de la FIFA a inversionistas privados, según declaró el domingo un portavoz del organismo mundial del fútbol. Infantino, que ya había anunciado que se presentaría a un cuarto mandato en marzo del año que viene, se ha enfrentado a peticiones de dimisión por parte de la UEFA, la AFC y la CONCACAF, después de que su plan de vender una participación del 20 % en el Mundial y otros eventos de la FIFA fuera descartado en julio ante la amplia reacción negativa que suscitó. No obstante, el presidente, de 56 años, sigue contando con el apoyo de las confederaciones africana y sudamericana. "El presidente de la FIFA anunció en abril que se presentará a la reelección en 2027. Por supuesto, nada ha cambiado. El señor Infantino se presentará a la reelección", declaró un portavoz de la FIFA en un comunicado. El comunicado se publicó después de que Infantino se mantuviera hermético cuando se le preguntó si se arrepentía de las turbulentas últimas seis semanas, mientras asistía el sábado al Mundial Sub-20 en Polonia. "Habrá mucho que decir, pero habrá un lugar y un momento adecuados para hacerlo", había dicho Infantino. Nadie ha anunciado oficialmente su candidatura para disputarle el puesto a Infantino en las elecciones del año que viene.

item.title: Nepali woman found alive days after family began mourning rites
item.description: Despite the devastation of the floods, rescuers have found people who survived extraordinary conditions, including Chandika Kumari Shrestha who survived in a narrow pocket of air in her collapsed home.
item.dc:creator: Adnan Abidi
item.content:encoded: Believing she had perished in Nepal's [USN:L1N44W056 TEXT:"deadly floods"], the family of Chandika Kumari Shrestha started the ritual of mourning the elderly woman's death. Ten days later, rescuers found her alive inside her collapsed home in the devastated Betrawati village, where she had survived in a narrow pocket of air amid water and mud. "The four-storey house was swept (away) by the floods and the house was left in the middle of a quicksand. While walking around it, we heard a voice 'save me,'" police officer Mahendra Darnal said. In a rescue operation on Saturday lasting 45 minutes, Darnal and his team found Shrestha in a confined space and sent her to an army hospital. "I was in touch with the family and they had started the 11-day mourning period," Darnal said. Shrestha was among the hundreds missing in Betrawati, an area among the hardest hit by the floods in Nepal and engulfed with white deposits compacted almost like concrete. Crews continue to recover scores of dead bodies. The town's market and most residential buildings, some as tall as four storeys, were almost completely buried under debris left by a torrent that swept through the valley, part of a disaster that killed more than 1,300 people across Nepal. Thousands remain unaccounted for. Rescue workers wearing hard hats were seen digging with shovels, while some were crawling through the gaps of collapsed buildings periodically blowing whistles to get the attention of anyone trapped and alive. Five days earlier, 24 bodies were found in a decomposed state in Betrawati's market area in a building that had contained a small shop, Darnal said. LOOKING FOR SIGNS OF LIFE Eleven days since a glacial collapse triggered the devastating floods, close to 5,000 are still missing. Hundreds of bodies have been swept onto the banks of rivers far from the ravaged Rasuwa district. In Chitwan, hundreds of miles away, several rounds of [USN:L1N44R01F TEXT:"mass burials"] have taken place for unidentified and badly decomposed bodies. Even as hope is beginning to fade, Nepal authorities continue their effort to look for people stuck in tunnels and under the thick deposits of mud that have hardened over buildings. Since Friday, they have pulled out [USN:L1N44W056 TEXT:"three people from the tunnels"], including a [USN:L4N44X01J TEXT:"Chinese citizen"] by the Trishuli river, where more than 900 are believed to be trapped. Others like Shrestha have survived in extraordinary conditions, including an [USN:L4N44P0XH TEXT:"8-year-old boy"] who was also reunited with his mother.

item.title: President Infantino will seek re-election in March, FIFA says
item.description: FIFA president Gianni Infantino remains committed to standing for re-election amid renewed opposition to his candidacy after a botched plan to sell a stake in FIFA competitions to private investors, a spokesperson for the global soccer body said on Sunday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: FIFA president Gianni Infantino remains committed to standing for re-election amid renewed opposition to his candidacy after [USN:L1N43X04P TEXT:"a botched plan"] to sell a stake in FIFA competitions to private investors, a spokesperson for the global soccer body said on Sunday. Infantino, who had previously announced that he would seek a fourth term in March next year, has faced calls to resign from UEFA, the AFC and CONCACAF, after his plan to sell a 20% stake in the World Cup and other FIFA events was scrapped amid widespread backlash in July. But the 56-year-old retains support from the African and South American confederations. "The FIFA president announced in April that he will stand for re-election in 2027. Of course, nothing has changed. Mr Infantino will be standing for re-election," a FIFA spokesperson said in a statement. The statement came after Infantino [USN:L1N44X02Z TEXT:"remained tight-lipped"] when asked whether he regretted the [USN:L6N44V19H TEXT:"turbulent last six weeks"] while attending the U-20 World Cup in Poland on Saturday. "There will be a lot to say, but there will be a right place and a right time to say this," Infantino had said. No one has formally announced a candidacy to challenge Infantino in next year's election.

item.title: Poland says suspected airspace violation caused by bird flock
item.description: Authorities in Poland said on Sunday that a suspected violation of the country's airspace originating on the other side of its border with neighbouring Belarus had been caused by a large flock of birds.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Authorities in Poland said on Sunday that a suspected violation of the country's airspace originating on the other side of its border with neighbouring Belarus had been caused by a large flock of birds. The event had prompted the Polish military to scramble helicopters to verify data of a possible violation registered by radiolocation systems shortly after noon local time (1000 GMT), a spokesman for Polish Armed Forces Operational Command told Reuters. "Indications recorded by the radar systems were not related to a violation of Polish airspace. They were caused by a large flock of birds, whose passage was recorded by airspace surveillance systems," the army later wrote on X. Poland's air traffic authority PANSA wrote in a separate post on X that Rzeszow Airport in southeastern Poland had resumed operations after they were briefly suspended in order to facilitate military aviation.

item.title: Gulf stocks end mixed as US-Iran tensions linger
item.description: Gulf stock markets ended mixed on Sunday, with traders treading carefully against the backdrop of an escalating standoff between Washington and Tehran.
item.dc:creator: Ateeq Shariff
item.content:encoded: Gulf stock markets ended mixed on Sunday, with traders treading carefully against the backdrop of an escalating standoff between Washington and Tehran. Iran has [USN:L1N44Y02B TEXT:"pledged"] to counter crippling U.S. sanctions while threatening a "painful response" to any further aggression. Six months after initial U.S.-Israeli strikes , the conflict remains at a stalemate as diplomatic peace efforts stall following the collapse of a June ceasefire. Meanwhile, tit-for-tat military action has resumed after a brief July lull, with U.S. Central Command confirming it struck three Iranian tankers on Saturday in retaliation for ballistic missile attacks on two U.S. Navy warships. Saudi Arabia's benchmark index (.TASI) edged 0.3% higher, bolstered by heavyweight lenders, as Al Rajhi Bank (1120.SE) gained 0.7% and Saudi National Bank (1180.SE) climbed 1.1%. In Qatar, the index (.QSI) lost 0.3%, hit by a 0.7% fall in Qatar Islamic Bank (QISB.QA) . Outside the Gulf, Egypt's blue-chip index (.EGX30) advanced 0.7%, led by a 2.2% rise in Talaat Moustafa Group Holding (TMGH.CA) . Saudi Arabia (.TASI) rose 0.3% to 11,069 Qatar (.QSI) eased 0.3% to 9,734 Egypt (.EGX30) gained 0.7% to 56,676 Bahrain (.BAX) down 0.1% to 1,937 Oman (.MSX30) was flat at 7,632 Kuwait (.BKP) lost 0.2% to 9,227

item.title: Astros aim to complete busy stretch with win vs. D-backs
item.description: The finale of their three-game interleague series with the visiting Arizona Diamondbacks on Sunday will mark the conclusion of a stretch of 13 games in 13 days for the Houston Astros.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: The finale of their three-game interleague series with the visiting Arizona Diamondbacks on Sunday will mark the conclusion of a stretch of 13 games in 13 days for the Houston Astros. The Astros' 4-3, 10-inning loss on Saturday did not impact their position in the American League West standings, as the Texas Rangers' home loss to the Tampa Bay Rays allowed Houston to maintain its three-game lead. Still, with a welcome day off coming on Monday, the Astros are laboring to cap this current stretch on a high note. "We have 20 games left," Astros manager Joe Espada said. "We're going to be facing some really good teams in September; they're aware of that. So they know we can rest later. Right now, we've got to stay locked in. "I'm so proud of the way they're playing. Once the game has started, they have been locked in and playing the game really hard." Right-hander Peter Lambert (8-7, 3.66 ERA) is scheduled to start the series rubber match for Houston (73-70). Lambert did not factor into the decision in a 6-3 win over the Chicago White Sox last Monday, allowing two runs on three hits and a season-high five walks with six strikeouts over 4 2/3 innings. Since earning his eighth win on July 11 against Texas, Lambert is 0-2 with a 4.63 ERA across nine starts. Lambert is 2-1 with a 3.79 ERA in six career appearances (two starts) against Arizona. In his previous appearance against the Diamondbacks on Aug 14, 2024, he allowed one unearned run on two hits and two walks with one strikeout over 2 1/3 innings in the Colorado Rockies' 11-4 loss. Left-hander Eduardo Rodriguez (14-5, 2.59) has the starting assignment for Arizona (75-68) on Sunday. Rodriguez is 5-0 with a 1.96 ERA over his last seven road starts, last losing away from home on May 15 in Colorado after allowing three runs on nine hits with six strikeouts over 5 1/3 innings. He had a four-start win streak snapped on Tuesday, allowing three runs on eight hits and three walks with three strikeouts over five innings in a 7-1 loss to the Philadelphia Phillies. Rodriguez, who owns a career winning percentage of 60.3, is 1-7 with a 6.67 ERA in 12 career starts against the Astros. In his previous start against Houston on July 22, 2025, Rodriguez tossed 6 1/3 shutout innings, allowing six hits and three walks while striking out three. He did not factor into the decision of a 3-1 home loss. The Diamondbacks are poised to welcome back right-handers Zac Gallen (right elbow inflammation) and Michael Soroka (right arm inflammation) from the 60-day and 15-day injured list, respectively, during the upcoming three-game interleague series at the Kansas City Royals. Gallen and Soroka are on the same timeline, leaving the D-backs with deployment options for both. Corbin Burnes is set to rejoin the rotation Tuesday following a 15-month recovery after Tommy John surgery, so potential bullpen usage is a factor as well. "Would we push one (back), which would give them seven days down, or do we piggyback them so they're both on the same day, which would most likely be Wednesday?" Diamondbacks manager Torey Lovullo said. "Those are the conversations we're having right now. How do we layer them back in? "They're both gassed up and ready to go. That piggyback situation could be perfectly timed on Wednesday. Those are the important conversations we're going to have. They both feel good." --Field Level Media

item.title: Iran's Hormuz leverage wanes as US economic squeeze bites
item.description: Tehran has failed to impose the costs it hoped would break Washington's resolve.
item.dc:creator: Samia Nakhoul
item.content:encoded: Six months after a conflict that rattled markets and pushed the Gulf to the brink of a wider war, the tide may be turning against Iran as Washington unleashes an unprecedented economic offensive to achieve what military force could not. After years of surviving sanctions, Tehran is now confronting one of the harshest squeezes in the Islamic Republic's history, according to Iranian insiders and regional sources. A U.S. naval blockade and [USN:L6N44T0TA TEXT:"tougher sanctions"] are curbing oil exports, restricting access to foreign currency and exposing growing strains in the economy. The campaign has led U.S. and regional officials to wager that mounting economic pressure can force Tehran to allow free passage through the Strait of Hormuz, which carries about a fifth of global oil and LNG supplies. Their bet rests on a simple calculation: Iran is suffering more economic damage than it is inflicting. Efforts to choke off oil exports have cut state revenues, while attempts to disrupt shipping through Hormuz have not triggered the global economic shock Tehran hoped would force Washington to compromise. Energy markets have adjusted and alternative supplies have continued to flow. "The balance of power has tilted against Iran a bit," said Iranian analyst Arash Azizi. Iran is losing some of the leverage it had over the Strait of Hormuz because it has been unable to close it fully, he said, adding that the U.S. naval blockade was "really hitting Iran." Azizi said Tehran had expected disruption in the strait to trigger a major shock to the global economy and drive Washington back to the negotiating table. "It hasn't happened, really," he said. Other countries had adapted, exposing limits to Iran's ability to inflict economic pain on the region and beyond. Whether the pressure will force concessions remains unclear, the regional sources said. Tehran has failed to impose the costs it hoped would break Washington's resolve but has shown little sign of abandoning demands for sanctions relief, access to frozen assets and recognition of its security role in Hormuz. Still, a new formula for resolving the standoff is now under discussion between mediators and Iran, the sources said. CAN TEHRAN OUTLAST THE SQUEEZE? Three senior Iranian sources acknowledged that Washington's campaign is becoming increasingly difficult to withstand. The latest measures have sharply restricted Tehran's ability to access foreign currency, import goods and tap global financing networks that have helped keep [USN:L1N44Y02B TEXT:"the economy"] afloat. Iranian leaders fear a worsening economy, marked by surging prices, weaker trade and pressure on household incomes, could reignite nationwide unrest that has repeatedly challenged the Islamic Republic. Shortages of key imports, including fuel and wheat, are becoming an increasing concern, officials said. U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent [USN:L6N44H0E8 TEXT:"described the strategy"] as a "one-two punch" combining the blockade with "the toughest sanctions in history." "It is going to work in Iran and we are going to collapse this regime," he told CNBC. For some U.S., Israeli and regional officials, such strains strengthen hopes that economic pressure could eventually carry political consequences inside Iran by triggering unrest, widening rifts within the leadership and weakening its grip on power. Others remain sceptical that economic and military coercion will produce a political rupture, pointing to decades of failed efforts to destabilise the Islamic Republic and Tehran's willingness to suppress dissent. They argue Iran's rulers may again prove more resilient than their adversaries expect. THE RESILIENCE TEST Dennis Ross, a former U.S. negotiator, said Washington may be interpreting Iran's economic distress as evidence of strategic success when the reality is more complicated. Tehran remains determined to demonstrate it can control Hormuz, but appears to be calibrating its use of force while keeping further escalation in reserve. The Revolutionary Guards may believe Iran can absorb the economic pain and outlast the pressure rather than compromise, Ross said. "The Iranians have consistently surprised us in terms of their resiliency," he added, saying he doubted economic and military pressure alone would force a retreat. Hardliners, he said, may believe they can endure and ultimately secure what they want. Resilience may depend as much on public tolerance as Tehran's ability to absorb economic hardship, said Burcu Ozcelik, a senior research fellow at the Royal United Services Institute. "Of course, the economic squeeze raises the risk of public unrest, but for now, a wartime mentality appears to have a significant hold over the population," said Ozcelik. "Foreign military intervention, civilian casualties and the perception of a wider civilization confrontation with a U.S.-led order are sustaining a degree of 'Iran-first' patriotic support, tolerance or simply patience with the regime." The result is a more stubborn impasse than Washington may have anticipated. Economic pressure is deepening the pain, but Tehran's powerful Revolutionary Guards may see endurance, backed by the threat of escalation, as leverage rather than a reason to concede. The key question is not whether Iran is hurting, but whether it is hurting enough to compromise before either side slips toward another confrontation, the regional sources said. Ross said the clearest path to a deal may lie in the dispute over shipping fees through the Strait of Hormuz. Iran could abandon any demand for a toll while retaining the right to charge for legitimate navigational, security or environmental services, he said. Such an arrangement could give both sides a claim to victory, allowing Tehran to step back without appearing to capitulate. "If you could announce that the Strait were reopened," Ross said, "I think Trump would do a deal."

item.title: Mets, Giants hope the power stays on in series finale
item.description: One of the biggest power outbursts of the season for the San Francisco Giants provided a glimpse at what could have been -- and what might be next season.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: One of the biggest power outbursts of the season for the San Francisco Giants provided a glimpse at what could have been -- and what might be next season. The Giants will look to build off a homer-heavy attack that powered a 9-5 victory on Saturday as they conclude their final series in the Eastern time zone on Sunday afternoon in Queens, N.Y. against the Mets. New York won the opener 10-6 on Friday. Giants left-hander Cesar Perdomo (0-0, 2.25 ERA) is slated to make his second big league appearance on Sunday when he starts against Mets right-hander Christian Scott (4-4, 3.80 ERA). Scott will be tasked with keeping the ball in the ballpark. Christian Koss and Rafael Devers both hit two homers Saturday for the Giants. Osleivis Basabe hit a two-run homer in the eighth and Grant McCray added a solo shot in the ninth for the Giants, whose six homers were one shy of their season high. San Francisco went deep seven times on June 5 in an 18-3 rout of the Chicago Cubs, when Willy Adames, Matt Chapman and Casey Schmitt had two homers apiece and Jonah Cox homered once. With Saturday's outburst, the Giants (59-84) have 164 homers this season, which puts them on pace for 185. San Francisco has hit at least 185 homers just once since Barry Bonds retired following the 2007 season. The 107-win 2021 squad went deep a franchise-record 241 times. The Giants' power output has been solid despite the long-term absences of Chapman (abdomen) and Schmitt (left knee), both of whom are out for the season. Adames hasn't played since Aug. 23 due to a sprained ligament in his left elbow. "There's some exciting names that aren't with us right now," Giants manager Tony Vitello said. Schmitt and Adames each have 21 homers -- tied for second on the team behind Devers, whose 35 homers put him within reach of becoming the first Giants slugger with 40 homers since Bonds hit 45 homers in 2004. The Mets (64-78) also have gotten a glimpse at a potentially brighter future in the power department during a disappointing season. New York tied a season-high with five homers in Friday's 10-6 win. The Mets have homered at least once in each of the last six games, a span in which they have 11 homers overall. The power surge began Aug. 30 -- one day after Juan Soto returned following a five-week stint on the injured list. Soto, Francisco Lindor and Marcus Semien, all of whom rank among the top 25 active players in career homers, have teamed up to hit 53 homers this season despite missing a combined 128 games. In addition, National League Rookie of the Year candidate Carson Benge (16 homers, 20 stolen bases) has a chance at a 20/20 season. Fellow rookie A.J. Ewing hit a two-run homer Saturday, when he also drew a pair of walks in four plate appearances. "I love the two walks as much as the home run," interim Mets manager Andy Green said. "I think that's indicative of him being in a good spot and trusting who he is." Perdomo made his major league debut on Tuesday when he allowed one run over four innings of relief as the Giants fell to the Pittsburgh Pirates, 13-12. Scott last pitched Aug. 28, when he took the defeat after giving up three runs over 5 1/3 innings in the Mets' 3-1 loss to the Houston Astros. Scott didn't factor into the decision in his lone start against the Giants on May 24, 2024, when he gave up two runs over six innings in the Mets' 8-7 loss. --Field Level Media

item.title: Pete Crow-Armstrong, Cubs seek series sweep of Marlins
item.description: The Chicago Cubs will look to strengthen their position atop the National League wild-card race on Sunday when they bid for a three-game sweep against the host Miami Marlins.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: The Chicago Cubs will look to strengthen their position atop the National League wild-card race on Sunday when they bid for a three-game sweep against the host Miami Marlins. Chicago (81-62) is led by center fielder Pete Crow-Armstrong, who is the current favorite to win National League Most Valuable Player Award. Armstrong has posted career-high totals in triples (seven), homers (39) and runs (105) to go along with 28 doubles, 94 RBIs, 33 steals and a .943 OPS. "Looking at Pete, he's the kind of player who is going to leave his mark in history," Cubs pitcher Shota Imanaga said of Armstrong, who needs one more homer to become the first Cub since Derrek Lee in 2005 to reach 40 in a season. "Having him behind me (defensively) means so much. Without Pete, we wouldn't be where we are." The Cubs lead the majors in several offensive statistics, including runs, walks, total bases, slugging percentage, OPS and homers. "Credit the Cubs," Marlins manager Clayton McCullough said following Saturday's 6-5 loss to Chicago. "It's a good lineup, not only with the ability to do damage but also how they work at-bats." Aside from Armstrong, three Cubs players have hit more than 20 homers: third baseman Alex Bregman (24); right fielder Seiya Suzuki (24); and left fielder Ian Happ (23). Middle infielder Nico Hoerner, with 22 steals, gives Chicago speed along with Armstrong. Chicago's pitching hasn't been as strong, entering the weekend ranked 17th in the majors in ERA. But acquiring Clay Holmes and David Peterson in two separate trades with the Mets have reinforced the pitching staff. The Mets also are the same franchise the Cubs used to acquire Armstrong and fellow outfielder Tyrone Taylor, who has been hot lately. Holmes (6-6, 2.09 ERA), Sunday's expected starter, scattered five hits over six scoreless innings in a 17-3 win over the Milwaukee Brewers last Monday. He is 3-1 with a 3.19 ERA in 13 career appearances (four starts) versus Miami. Meanwhile, the Marlins (71-72) are in contention but currently four games outside of a wild-card playoff berth. Miami will start right-hander Tyler Phillips (4-6, 3.43). Phillips, 28, has pitched just one inning against the Cubs, allowing two hits and no runs on May 21, 2025. For his career, Phillips is much better as a reliever (2.49 ERA in 71 appearances) than as a starter (5.12 ERA in 24 games). On the positive side for Phillips, he has a better career ERA at home (2.83) than on the road (4.86). Miami's bullpen is a bit thin due to injuries to closer Pete Fairbanks and set-up man Anthony Bender. In addition, second baseman Xavier Edwards is out due to a thumb injury. But players such as Griffin Conine and Kyle Stowers -- who both homered on Saturday -- have stepped up for Miami. Conine has been an especially good story as he is finally shedding his injuries. "Griffin has earned the opportunities he's getting," McCullough said. "His at-bat quality is getting better. I'm not surprised with his power (15 homers in 75 games)." --Field Level Media

item.title: La OPEP+ mantiene sin cambios su política de producción de petróleo para octubre
item.description: La OPEP+ mantuvo sin cambios su política de producción de petróleo para octubre en una reunión celebrada el domingo, según indicó en un comunicado, ya que el grupo de productores debe acordar nuevas cuotas antes de decidir sus próximos pasos en materia de producción.
item.dc:creator: Ahmad Ghaddar, Olesya Astakhova, Alex Lawler
item.content:encoded: La OPEP+ mantuvo sin cambios su política de producción de petróleo para octubre en una reunión celebrada el domingo, según indicó en un comunicado, ya que el grupo de productores debe acordar nuevas cuotas antes de decidir sus próximos pasos en materia de producción. La reunión de los siete miembros principales de la OPEP+ —Arabia Saudita, Rusia, Irak, Kuwait, Argelia, Kazajistán y Omán— se produce mientras la guerra en Irán sigue perturbando las exportaciones de petróleo a través del estrecho de Ormuz, lo que limita la influencia de la OPEP+ sobre los precios y la cuota de mercado. En agosto, la OPEP+ acordó el aumento de la producción para septiembre, completando así la retirada gradual del recorte de suministro de 1,65 millones de barriles diarios acordado inicialmente en 2023. A pesar de los aumentos de producción acordados, el grupo formado por la Organización de Países Exportadores de Petróleo y sus aliados, entre ellos Rusia, sigue produciendo muy por debajo de sus objetivos debido a la guerra. EL PODER DE LA OPEP, LIMITADO POR EL CONFLICTO CON IRÁN «La OPEP+ tiene actualmente un poder muy limitado sobre el mercado físico del petróleo», afirmó Jorge León, de Rystad Energy. «El grupo puede modificar los objetivos de producción sobre el papel, pero no puede garantizar que esos barriles se produzcan o lleguen realmente al mercado». «La atención se aleja ahora de los ajustes mensuales de producción y se centra en el debate, mucho más trascendental, sobre 2027». La OPEP+ sigue aplicando otra ronda de recortes de producción, que afecta a la mayoría de los miembros del grupo de 21 países hasta finales de 2026. Antes de que el grupo decida cómo retirar los recortes y devolver la producción al mercado, debe revisar la capacidad de producción de petróleo de sus miembros para establecer las bases de referencia de producción para 2027, que constituyen la base de las cuotas. Es probable que este debate tenga lugar a finales de 2026 y, por lo tanto, es probable que la OPEP+ suspenda sus aumentos de producción durante el cuarto trimestre, según informaron anteriormente fuentes a Reuters. La declaración del domingo no hizo mención alguna a la política más allá de octubre. Solo los siete miembros de la OPEP+ que se reunieron el domingo, más los Emiratos Árabes Unidos hasta que abandonaron la OPEP en mayo, han participado en las decisiones mensuales sobre la producción en los últimos años. Estos siete países celebrarán su próxima reunión el 4 de octubre.

item.title: At least 25 killed in bus crash on Cape Verde's Fogo island, agency says
item.description: At least 25 people, many of them schoolchildren and teenagers, were killed when a bus plunged into a ravine on Fogo, one of Cape Verde's islands in the Atlantic Ocean off the coast of West Africa, national news agency Inforpress reported on Sunday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: At least 25 people, many of them schoolchildren and teenagers, were killed when a bus plunged into a ravine on Fogo, one of Cape Verde's islands in the Atlantic Ocean off the coast of West Africa, national news agency Inforpress reported on Sunday. The crash occurred on a mountain road in northern Fogo late on Saturday, when the bus veered off the road and plunged about 30 metres into a steep ravine, it said. Many of those on board were primary and secondary school students, the agency said. Several injured passengers were taken to Sao Francisco de Assis Regional Hospital on Fogo. Education officials said the outing was not organised by local schools but was an annual trip privately arranged by the driver, who was among those killed, Inforpress said.

item.title: Tigers look for parting shot at Guardians in finale of season series
item.description: The high point of the Detroit Tigers' season came against the Cleveland Guardians on Aug. 13, when they moved into a share of an American League wild-card spot with a home win.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: The high point of the Detroit Tigers' season came against the Cleveland Guardians on Aug. 13, when they moved into a share of an American League wild-card spot with a home win. Their low point did, as well, as Cleveland's two walk-off wins in a doubleheader sweep Friday essentially knocked the Tigers out of the postseason hunt. Detroit gets its final shot at the Guardians this year on Sunday afternoon, when the teams wrap up a four-game series in Cleveland. Tigers right-hander Jackson Jobe (1-2, 4.63 ERA) will get the start against Guardians righty Gavin Williams (13-7, 3.81). Three-time All-Star Riley Greene gave the visitors a bit of payback on Saturday, amassing a career-high tying four hits, four RBIs, three runs and two homers in leading Detroit to a 6-0 rout of Cleveland. It was the ninth multi-homer game of his five-year career and his first blasts anywhere since spending 20 days on the injured list with a strained right hamstring. Greene's seven home runs in Cleveland are his most in any visiting ballpark. "We come here all the time, so maybe that's the reason why," Greene said, laughing. "It's baseball. It happens. After what happened last night, you just have to flush it and get to the next day." The Guardians (72-71) are now even with the Toronto Blue Jays in the battle for the final AL wild-card position, but Cleveland loses the head-to-head tiebreaker. Detroit (65-77) is 6 1/2 games behind them with 20 to play. Greene had been 1-for-13 since being activated, but came to life against his offseason buddy, Guardians All-Star pitcher Parker Messick. The homers totaled 828 feet and each landed atop the high wall in left-center field. "I think he owes me a fishing trip that we've been talking about the last few times I've seen him," Messick quipped. "To go backside, left-center field is just a really good swing. I throw those balls there to a lot of other lefties and don't get that same result." There won't be any hard feelings the next time they hang out in Florida, though. Greene said it didn't matter who he was hitting against, he was desperate to get back in a groove. "I just had to get good pitches to hit and was trying to get on strikes," Greene said. "On the first one, I was just trying to find barrels and make something happen." Jobe has either been terrific or terrible in five starts, all coming since Aug. 8 as the Tigers have fallen apart. Three of them have seen him allow one or fewer runs, but he was rocked for 10 earned runs in 8 2/3 combined innings during the other two. His only career game against the Guardians was a home loss on May 23, 2025, when he gave up two runs in five innings. Greene's big night coincided with Framber Valdez and two relievers tossing a three-hitter. Angel Martinez, David Fry and Angel Genao each had a single as Cleveland was shut out for the 15th time, tied for the most in the majors with the Cincinnati Reds and Pittsburgh Pirates. "That's the most four-seam (fastballs Valdez has) used, almost 20%," Guardians manager Stephen Vogt said. "That's not something he historically does. The two fastballs, and he threw just enough off-speed, to keep us off of that." Williams last pitched on Sept. 1, holding Toronto without an earned run in seven innings of a 6-1 victory. It was one of four wins by Cleveland in nine games on its homestand that ends Sunday. Nicknamed "The Big Rig," Williams has not faced Detroit this season. He is 3-2 with a 1.88 ERA in seven career starts against the Central Division rival. "We capitalized (Friday) night, right? Then today, we got beat by a very good pitcher," Vogt said. "That was the story, and we'll be ready Sunday." --Field Level Media

item.title: Irán abordará problemas económicos y advierte de que los nuevos ataques serán "más dolorosos"
item.description: Irán ha afirmado que intensificará sus esfuerzos para hacer frente a los problemas provocados por las sanciones estadounidenses que están paralizando su economía, mientras que un alto cargo iraní ha advertido de una "respuesta dolorosa" si el país sufre nuevos ataques.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Irán ha afirmado que intensificará sus esfuerzos para hacer frente a los problemas provocados por las sanciones estadounidenses que están paralizando su economía, mientras que un alto cargo iraní ha advertido de una "respuesta dolorosa" si el país sufre nuevos ataques. Seis meses después de los ataques de Estados Unidos e Israel contra Irán, la guerra parece estar en un punto muerto. El acuerdo preliminar de alto el fuego alcanzado en junio se ha desmoronado y se han logrado pocos avances en los esfuerzos diplomáticos para volver a encarrilar el proceso de paz. Tras una pausa en las acciones militares durante gran parte de agosto, se han reanudado los ataques de represalia: el Mando Central de Estados Unidos ha afirmado que el sábado atacó tres petroleros iraníes en respuesta al lanzamiento de misiles balísticos por parte del Cuerpo de la Guardia Revolucionaria Islámica de Irán contra dos buques de la Armada de Estados Unidos. Tras los ataques, el presidente del Parlamento iraní, Mohammad Baqer Qalibaf, declaró el domingo que Estados Unidos debería comprender que las reglas del juego en la guerra contra Irán han cambiado "antes de que sea demasiado tarde". "A partir de ahora, cualquier ataque contra los intereses y la seguridad de Irán recibirá una respuesta más rápida, más contundente y más dolorosa", afirmó en un discurso publicado en su canal de Telegram. Teherán ha demostrado que sigue conservando la capacidad de atacar los intereses estadounidenses en los países vecinos y de bloquear el flujo de petróleo a través del estrecho de Ormuz, por donde circulaba una quinta parte del suministro mundial de petróleo antes del conflicto. SANCIONES Y EL BLOQUEO PETROLÍFERO ASFIXIAN LA ECONOMÍA Sin embargo, la campaña de Estados Unidos para estrangular la economía iraní mediante el bloqueo de sus exportaciones de petróleo y la lucha contra la elusión de sanciones resulta cada vez más difícil de soportar, según han afirmado tres fuentes iraníes de alto rango. En su discurso del domingo, Qalibaf añadió que, junto al frente militar, la principal batalla de Irán se libraba ahora en torno a la producción y los medios de subsistencia de la población. Mencionó las fuertes fluctuaciones monetarias, la inflación, el desempleo y la gestión del mercado como retos principales, y añadió que los iraníes podían tolerar las penurias, pero no la mala gestión ni la inacción, y esperaban que el Gobierno actuara con rapidez. El ministro de Economía de Irán, Ali Madanizadeh, afirmó que Teherán tenía previsto responder a la presión económica de Estados Unidos con reformas y rechazó la idea de que las sanciones le hicieran cambiar de rumbo, según informaron el domingo los medios estatales. "Hablan de presión económica y aislamiento, de romper los lazos financieros, y creen que, al ejercer presión sobre la economía de un país, pueden cambiar las decisiones de su pueblo", afirmó Madanizadeh. "Tengo que aclarar un punto: la responsabilidad de reformar la economía de Irán recae en su Gobierno y su pueblo, no en el Tesoro de Estados Unidos". Por otra parte, el viceministro de Economía, Morteza Zamanian, declaró el domingo que el "Cuartel General de la Guerra Económica" del ministerio estaba redoblando sus esfuerzos para resolver los problemas causados por la guerra, según la agencia de noticias semioficial Tasnim. ISLA DE KHARG HA SUFRIDO 550 ATAQUES EN LOS ÚLTIMOS MESES, SEGÚN IRÁN Irán es el tercer mayor productor de la Organización de Países Exportadores de Petróleo y, antes de la guerra, exportaba el 90 % de su crudo a través de su centro de exportación de la isla de Kharg. Los flujos se han visto interrumpidos desde que, a mediados de abril, comenzó el bloqueo estadounidense a las exportaciones de petróleo iraní. El 31 de agosto, Trump publicó un mensaje de una sola línea en las redes sociales acompañado de un vídeo generado por IA en el que se veía cómo la isla de Kharg "volaba en mil pedazos". Las autoridades iraníes han prometido una respuesta contundente si Kharg es atacada. En una entrevista emitida el domingo en la televisión estatal, el ministro de Petróleo de Irán, Mohsen Paknejad, afirmó que la isla había sido alcanzada unas 550 veces en los meses anteriores, pero que seguía en funcionamiento. Irán también ha impuesto un bloqueo en el estrecho de Ormuz, lo que supone un problema para el presidente de Estados Unidos, Donald Trump, al provocar un aumento de los precios del combustible a nivel mundial de cara a las elecciones de mitad de mandato de su Partido Republicano en noviembre. El sábado, el Mando Central de Estados Unidos afirmó que había atacado tres buques iraníes, incluido uno frente a la costa de la isla de Kharg, después de que el Cuerpo de la Guardia Revolucionaria Islámica de Irán lanzara misiles balísticos contra dos buques de la Armada de Estados Unidos. "Que el mensaje al IRGC quede claro: si disparan contra dos de nuestros buques, os impondremos un coste económico aún mayor: derribaremos tres de los vuestros", afirmó el almirante Brad Cooper, jefe del Mando Central de Estados Unidos, que supervisa las fuerzas armadas estadounidenses en Oriente Medio.

item.title: Ukraine-Les Américains Witkoff et Kushner à Kyiv après Moscou
item.description: Les émissaires américains Steve Witkoff et Jared Kushner ont rencontré dimanche à Kyiv le président ukrainien Volodimir Zelensky au lendemain d'un entretien à Moscou avec le président russe Vladimir Poutine, dans le cadre d'une nouvelle tentative des Etats-Unis de mettre fin à quatre ans et demi de guerre entre l'Ukraine et la Russie.
item.dc:creator: Max Hunder, Anna Voitenko
item.content:encoded: Les émissaires américains Steve Witkoff et Jared Kushner ont rencontré dimanche à Kyiv le président ukrainien Volodimir Zelensky au lendemain d'un entretien à Moscou avec le président russe Vladimir Poutine, dans le cadre d'une nouvelle tentative des Etats-Unis de mettre fin à quatre ans et demi de guerre entre l'Ukraine et la Russie. Devant la presse à Kyiv, Steve Witkoff a fait savoir que l'équipe américaine se sentait "très encouragée" par ce qu'il a qualifié de discussion "substantielle et importante". Jared Kushner a émis le souhait de parvenir à de nouveaux progrès dans les pourparlers de paix. Volodimir Zelensky a indiqué pour sa part que d'autres pourparlers, auxquels participeraient des représentants européens, étaient prévus plus tard ce dimanche. Des conseillers à la sécurité nationale britannique, français et allemand se trouvaient à Kyiv ce dimanche. Le président américain Donald Trump, qui avait affirmé avant son retour à la Maison blanche en 2024 qu'il trouverait rapidement une issue au conflit, a laissé entendre vendredi que Washington avait une nouvelle proposition à soumettre à ces deux pays, sans plus de précisions. Ses précédentes initiatives n'ont débouché sur aucune avancée significative et ses représentants semblent une nouvelle fois ne guère avoir progressé lors de leur rencontre de trois heures samedi avec Vladimir Poutine. Le conseiller du Kremlin Iouri Ouchakov a néanmoins qualifié cet entretien de "fortement utile" et un responsable de la Maison blanche a dit à Reuters que de nouvelles annonces seraient faites dans les prochaines semaines. Avant sa rencontre avec Steve Witkoff et Jared Kushner en compagnie d'autres responsables ukrainiens de haut rang dans le centre de Kyiv, Volodimir Zelensky a dit sur les réseaux sociaux la volonté de l'Ukraine de mettre fin à la guerre. "Des garanties de sécurité sont nécessaires. Une paix digne après la guerre est nécessaire. Nous avons formulé des propositions", a déclaré le président ukrainien. Volodimir Zelensky considère que l'implication des Etats-Unis est indispensable à tout accord. Il pense qu'il existe une fenêtre d'opportunité pour conclure une paix avec la Russie avant que la classe politique américaine ne bascule bientôt vers la prochaine élection présidentielle de 2028 aux Etats-Unis. ESPOIRS Steve Witkoff et Jared Kushner se sont déjà rendus à plusieurs reprises à Moscou en tant que médiateurs mais il s'agit de leur première visite à Kyiv. Cette venue nourrit les espoirs de certains habitants de la capitale ukrainienne, bombardée sans relâche par la Russie depuis plusieurs semaines. "Le problème peut être réglé en un clin d'oeil. Nous voulons la paix. J'ai moi-même combattu donc je sais ce qu'est la guerre. Nous avons besoin de la paix car il n'y a pas d'autre issue", dit Stepan Yermak, un ancien combattant. Svitlana Kurylenko, serveuse dans un café, espère pour sa part "un accord qui ne sera jamais rompu". "Qu'on laisse l'Ukraine tranquille et son peuple vivre en paix", dit cette jeune femme de 19 ans. Russes et Ukrainiens affichent cependant des positions impossibles à réconcilier en l'état, aussi bien sur le plan territorial avec des revendications de Moscou sur des régions ukrainiennes que Kyiv refuse de céder, que sur l'avenir même de l'Ukraine et ses volontés de rapprochement avec l'Union européenne et l'Otan. Si le front des combats évolue peu au sol, la Russie et l'Ukraine ont intensifié leurs frappes aériennes dans la profondeur depuis plusieurs semaines. La Russie a néanmoins annoncé une pause de ses bombardements sur Kyiv jusqu'à lundi et Volodimir Zelensky a déclaré que l'Ukraine s'abstiendrait également de viser Moscou sur cette période. L'armée russe a tout de même poursuivi sa campagne de bombardements sur d'autres villes ukrainiennes samedi tandis que les forces ukrainiennes ont dit dimanche avoir frappé dans la nuit une raffinerie à Riazan, à près de 500 km de la frontière. Le ministère russe de la Défense a annoncé dimanche que ses forces avaient frappé en mer Noire un cargo ukrainien chargé de matériel militaire fourni à l'armée ukrainienne par des pays occidentaux, ont rapporté les agences de presse russes.

item.title: Pirates' Paul Skenes faces childhood favorite Angels in series finale
item.description: Paul Skenes has started two All-Star Games, won an ERA title and garnered the 2025 National League Cy Young Award. But one thing the hard-throwing right-hander hasn't done in his career is pitch against the team he rooted for while growing up in southern California.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Paul Skenes has started two All-Star Games, won an ERA title and garnered the 2025 National League Cy Young Award. But one thing the hard-throwing right-hander hasn't done in his career is pitch against the team he rooted for while growing up in southern California. That will change Sunday afternoon when Skenes (9-11, 3.97 ERA) takes the mound for the Pittsburgh Pirates (70-73) when they host the Los Angeles Angels (54-88) in the rubber game of their three-game series. Skenes starred for El Toro High School in Lake Forest, Calif., about a 25-minute drive south of Angel Stadium. It's the same high school that produced a pair of pretty talented major league third basemen named Nolan Arenado and Matt Chapman. Skenes brings a seven-start winless streak into the contest after picking up a no-decision in his last start on Tuesday against San Francisco. He left after allowing five runs, including a three-run homer by Rafael Devers, on eight hits over 4 2/3 innings. He walked three, struck out four and departed with a six-run lead after throwing 95 pitches, 56 for strikes. "I feel good. I think I could have gone longer," Skenes said afterward. "I don't know how many pitches I threw today, but I know they're trying to watch volume a little bit, so I'm not pushing back too much." Skenes' last win came on July 19 in a 7-1 victory at Cleveland. Pittsburgh, trying to capture its fourth straight series, needs a win to keep its slim National League playoff hopes alive. The Pirates are five games out of the final wild-card spot with only 19 games remaining. Right-hander Walbert Urena (9-9, 2.85 ERA), expected to receive some down-ballot votes for A.L. Rookie of the Year, gets the start for Los Angeles. Urena, who has yielded just a .203 batting average in 23 starts, comes in off arguably the best start of his career in a 10-1 victory over the New York Yankees. He allowed one run on five hits in seven innings with no walks and tied his career high with eight strikeouts. "No panic when you watch him," Angels manager Kurt Suzuki said of the 22-year-old Urena. "When you face the Yankees and the Phillies and the Red Sox and teams like that, there's always a little bit of a sense of anxiety and when you watch Walby from pitch one, it was zero anxiety. I think it was (11 straight strikes to start the game). That's the sign of an ace. I thought he pitched great tonight." Los Angeles, trying to avoid the first 100-loss season in franchise history, bounced back from a 1-0 loss in Friday's series opener to defeat the Pirates, 6-1, on Saturday. Yusei Kikuchi allowed five hits over six innings and struck out six en route to his first victory since Sept. 24, 2025 against Kansas City. Josh Lowe homered, Wade Meckler had a pair of doubles and two RBIs and Zach Neto went 3-for-5 with an RBI and a run scored to lead the Angels. Los Angeles got a bit of a scare when Mike Trout, who went 2-for-4 with a run scored and an RBI, was hit on the left hand by a Yohan Ramirez sweeper in the ninth inning and was lifted for pinch-runner Jose Siri. Trout underwent X-rays after the game, which came back negative. -Field Level Media

item.title: Orioles eager to halt 'frustrating' stretch in finale vs. Red Sox
item.description: The Baltimore Orioles need to generate offense to have any chance to win games, and that's even more clear after the past two outings.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: The Baltimore Orioles need to generate offense to have any chance to win games, and that's even more clear after the past two outings. They've failed to score in a pair of consecutive shutout defeats to the visiting Boston Red Sox. The Red Sox (78-65) will vie for a four-game series sweep of the Orioles on Sunday afternoon. "They're making pitches, and to their credit," Orioles first baseman Pete Alonso said. "But also for us, I don't think we're necessarily capitalizing the most when we get pitches in the zone. It's really frustrating for sure." The Orioles (69-74) will look to shed a five-game skid. "We've been here before, and for our guys it's just regrouping, trusting each other, playing for each other," Baltimore manager Craig Albernaz said. "Passing the baton. That's when we're at our best, when we're playing that team approach, nine versus one against the starter." After having Saturday night off, former Orioles catcher Adley Rutschman figures to be back behind the plate for Boston. He homered twice in the series opener in a much-anticipated return to Baltimore. Until that offensive outburst against the Orioles, Rutschman's biggest contributions and much of his focus had been on the defensive side. He said he knows that's important going forward as well. "Making sure that everything's running smoothly from the catching side, and that's kind of been the biggest thing as far as workload goes," Rutschman said. "Making sure I'm doing those guys a good service when I'm behind the plate." Boston's starters haven't allowed a run in back-to-back games. "Second night in a row we've got the starter out there through seven innings," Red Sox manager Chad Tracy said following Saturday night's 5-0 victory. Boston has named left-hander Payton Tolle (8-6, 3.23 ERA) as its starter for Sunday's game. He's 4-0 in his last 10 starts, though he's without a decision in his past three outings. Tolle has given the Red Sox at least five innings in eight consecutive starts, beginning July 20 when he allowed four runs in 5 2/3 innings to the Orioles in a no-decision -- though a game Boston won. The Red Sox also won June 3 at home when Tolle blanked the Orioles for six innings. Those are the only times Tolle has faced Baltimore in two big-league seasons. Right-hander Kyle Bradish (7-12, 4.01) will be the starting pitcher for the Orioles. He has gone seven consecutive starts without a victory, posting a 0-3 mark during that stretch. His last victory came when he held the Red Sox to one run in six innings July 22 in Boston, though he took the loss during an April meeting at home versus the Red Sox. In 11 career starts against the Red Sox, he's 2-6 with a 6.12 ERA. Much might be asked of Bradish and any other Baltimore pitchers if the Orioles can't crank up some offense. "Seems like our guys are offensively pressing a little bit, trying to do too much," Albernaz said. "Not everyone and it's not every single at-bat. It's just, you just see they're trying, they know where we're at. They're trying to come through for the team and come through for the rest of the boys, and sometimes it works out where they put together some good swings." --Field Level Media

item.title: Iran to tackle economic issues, says further attacks will be 'more painful'
item.description: The U.S. campaign to throttle Iran's economy by blockading its oil exports and stopping sanctions evasion is growing increasingly difficult to withstand, three senior Iranian sources said.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Iran said it will step up efforts to tackle problems created by the U.S. sanctions that are [USN:L8N44W0VU TEXT:"crippling its economy"], while a senior Iranian official warned of a "painful response" if it comes under further attack. Six months after U.S.-Israeli strikes against Iran, the war appears to be at a stalemate. A preliminary ceasefire accord reached in June has unravelled and little progress has been made in diplomatic efforts to get the peace process back on track. After a pause in military action for much of August, tit-for-tat strikes have resumed with U.S. Central Command saying it hit three [USN:L1N44Y028 TEXT:"Iranian tankers"] on Saturday after Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps launched ballistic missiles at two U.S. Navy ships. Following the attacks, Iran's Parliament Speaker Mohammad Baqer Qalibaf said on Sunday that the U.S. should understand that the rules of the game in the war against Iran have changed "before it is too late". "From now on, any attack against Iran’s interests and security will receive a faster, heavier and more painful response,” he said in a speech published on his Telegram channel. Tehran has shown it retains the capability to attack U.S. interests in neighbouring countries and to shut down oil flows through the Strait of Hormuz, through which a fifth of global oil supplies flowed prior to the conflict. SANCTIONS, OIL BLOCKADE SQUEEZE ECONOMY However, the U.S. campaign to throttle Iran's economy by blockading its oil exports and stopping sanctions evasion is growing increasingly [USN:L1N44W081 TEXT:"difficult to withstand"], three senior Iranian sources have said. In his speech on Sunday, Qalibaf added that alongside the military front, Iran’s main battle was now over production and people’s livelihoods. He cited sharp currency fluctuations, inflation, unemployment and market management as major challenges, adding Iranians could tolerate hardship but not mismanagement or inaction and expected the government to act quickly. Iran's Economy Minister Ali Madanizadeh said that Tehran planned to respond to U.S. economic pressure with reforms and rejected the notion that sanctions would cause it to change course, according to state media on Sunday. “They speak of economic pressure and isolation, of breaking off financial ties and they think that by pressuring the economy of a country they can change the decisions of its people,” Madanizadeh said. “I have to clarify one point: the responsibility of reforming Iran’s economy is with its government and people, not with the U.S. Treasury." Separately, Economy Ministry deputy Morteza Zamanian said on Sunday that the ministry's “Economic War Headquarters” was doubling down on its work to resolve problems caused by the war, according to the semi-official Tasnim news agency. KHARG ISLAND HIT 550 TIMES IN PRIOR MONTHS, IRAN SAYS Iran is the third-largest producer in the Organization of the Petroleum Exporting Countries and exported 90% of its crude via its [USN:L1N44S09M TEXT:"Kharg Island"] export hub before the war. Flows have been disrupted since a U.S. blockade of Iranian oil exports began in mid-April. On Sunday, U.S. Central Command said on X that as of September 6 it had redirected 92 commercial vessels, disabled three and boarded two to ensure strict compliance with its blockade. On August 31, Trump issued a one-line social media post accompanied by an AI-generated video depicting Kharg Island being "blown to smithereens." Iranian authorities have vowed a strong response if Kharg is attacked. In an interview aired on state TV on Sunday, Iran's Oil Minister Mohsen Paknejad said the island had been hit around 550 times in previous months but continued to operate. Iran has also imposed a blockade on the Strait of Hormuz, creating an issue for U.S. President Donald Trump by pushing up fuel prices globally ahead of midterm elections for his Republican Party in November. However, U.S. Energy Secretary Chris Wright said oil was getting through the waterway. "Our transits through the Strait are averaging over 9 million barrels a day now, and with the access pipelines that go around the Strait, we're probably two thirds or more of pre-conflict flows. So Iranians are still causing trouble, but the United States Navy is winning that battle," he told CNN. On Saturday, U.S. Central Command said it struck three Iranian vessels, including one off the coast of Kharg Island, after Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps launched ballistic missiles at two U.S. Navy ships. The IRGC responded by threatening intensified strikes against U.S. military vessels in the region, and said later it targeted the three tankers as well as three U.S.-linked vessels in other areas. Tasnim, the semi-official Iranian news agency, had reported that four U.S. missiles hit a tanker in the area of Kharg's anchorage. Tasnim quoted local sources as saying there were no casualties and the tanker's crew was being evacuated. No American personnel were harmed, Central Command said. On Sunday, Tasnim reported that the IRGC had shot down a U.S. surveillance balloon over Erbil in northern Iraq, describing it as part of a broader effort to eliminate U.S. aerial surveillance and early-warning systems in the region.

item.title: US envoys make first Kyiv visit amid Ukraine war peace push
item.description: The U.S. envoys arrived from Moscow where they held three hours of talks with Vladimir Putin, but did not appear to secure a breakthrough in the conflict.
item.dc:creator: Max Hunder, Anna Voitenko
item.content:encoded: U.S. peace envoys Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff met with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy in Kyiv on Sunday as the Trump administration renewed its push to end Russia's four-and-a-half-year war in Ukraine . Kushner and Witkoff travelled from Moscow, where they [USN:L1N44X01Y TEXT:"held three hours of talks"] with Russian President Vladimir Putin on Saturday but did not appear to secure a breakthrough in the conflict. Previous rounds of U.S.-mediated peace talks encouraged by President Donald Trump , who campaigned on a promise to quickly end the war, have yielded few results. He [USN:L1N44W0SY TEXT:"suggested"] on Friday that the U.S. had a fresh proposal though he did not elaborate. Kremlin aide Yuri Ushakov described Saturday's meeting as "highly useful", while a White House official told Reuters that next steps would be announced in the coming weeks. The two envoys met Zelenskiy and other top Ukrainian officials in central Kyiv. Zelenskiy, who believes Washington will be key to any peace deal, has said a window of opportunity to make peace exists before the U.S. begins focusing on its next presidential election. After the first round of talks between Ukrainian and U.S. negotiators that lasted about three hours, the U.S. envoys said that they were looking forward to making more progress. "Substantive, important, and we are very encouraged,” Witkoff told reporters after the talks, which also included a working lunch. Zelenskiy said that more talks, which would also include European representatives, were planned later on Sunday. British, French and German national security advisers were in Kyiv on Sunday. "Security guarantees are needed. A dignified post-war peace is needed. Our proposals have been drawn up," Zelenskiy said as his negotiating team was preparing to meet U.S. envoys. CAUTIOUS OPTIMISM ON THE STREETS OF KYIV Witkoff and Kushner, Trump's son-in-law, have visited Moscow several times in their roles as peace envoys. But Sunday is their first visit to Kyiv in their capacity as U.S. negotiators. Their visit has long been sought by Ukraine's leadership, and on the streets of Kyiv, which has been bombarded heavily in recent weeks, some residents were hopeful. "The issue can be solved in the blink of an eye. We want peace. I've fought myself, so I know what war is like. We need peace, because there's no other way," said military veteran Stepan Yermak. In previous talks, the sides have remained far apart on key issues, including the future of the eastern Ukrainian region of Donbas. Russia has demanded Ukraine's withdrawal from an entrenched belt of towns that it still controls there, but Kyiv has refused, reasoning that it can still hold on. For Ukraine, hard security guarantees from its European allies and the U.S. are crucial to deterring Russia from invading again. "We need an agreement that will never be broken," said Svitlana Kurylenko, a 19-year-old cafe worker. "Just leave Ukraine alone and let people live in peace." TEMPORARY HALT IN STRIKES Though the front lines of the ground war remain largely static, both Russian and Ukrainian forces have intensified long-range air strikes in recent weeks. Russia has pounded the Ukrainian capital day and night with missiles and drones for the past two weeks, including an [USN:L1N44W0FE TEXT:"attack on Friday"] on the headquarters of the SBU security service. The Kremlin has said it would pause strikes on Kyiv until Monday, while Zelenskiy has said Ukraine would also halt strikes on Moscow. There was no let-up in fighting along the 1,200-km (750-mile) front, however, and Russia bombarded other Ukrainian cities on Saturday. Ukraine has inflicted damaging hits throughout the summer on Russian refineries, oil terminals and the warehouses of online retailer Wildberries, in an attempt to raise the cost to Moscow of continuing the war. Ukraine said on Sunday it had struck the Ryazan oil refinery, around 480 km (300 miles) inside Russia, overnight, causing a fire.

item.title: China to pump $54 billion into state banks, insurers in capital-boosting push
item.description: Beijing is making the coordinated push to shore up capital across its financial system as weak loan demand remains a drag on the world's second-largest economy.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: China's finance ministry will lead a combined $54 billion capital injections into state-owned insurers and banks, the companies said on Sunday, in a coordinated push by Beijing to shore up capital across its financial system. China Life Insurance (Group) Co, the country's largest life insurer, will receive 35 billion yuan ($5.2 billion), while China Taiping Insurance Group will get 7 billion yuan, the two groups said in statements. Separately People's Insurance Company (Group) of China (601319.SS) said it planned to raise up to 15 billion yuan through a private placement of A-shares to the Ministry of Finance, with the proceeds to be used to replenish its capital. The initiative could help bolster state insurers that were directed to [USN:P8N3NE00R TEXT:"support the stock market"] with medium- and long-term funds, while positioning them to help regulators manage smaller, higher-risk insurance companies. FINANCIAL SECTOR STABILITY The insurance sector has been grappling with eroding profitability due to persistently low interest rates, with numerous small and mid-sized insurers reporting deteriorating solvency ratios. China Export and Credit Insurance Corp also said the finance ministry will inject 10 billion yuan to boost its core capital, and China Reinsurance (Group) said it will raise 3 billion yuan. "The injection is an important step by the country to enhance the financial sector's ability to serve the real economy and promote the high-quality development of the financial and insurance industries," China Life said in its statement, adding that it would strengthen the group's ability to withstand risks. Taiping said the funds would bolster its solvency and other key indicators. BANKS TAP RECAPITALISATION PLAN Separately, three state lenders on Sunday also announced they will receive a combined 290 billion yuan in capital injections. The plan was first [USN:L4N3ZS0O1 TEXT:"unveiled"] at an annual parliamentary meeting in March this year, extending a financing tool that had helped bolster some other big state banks [USN:L3N3QE05W TEXT:"last year"]. Agricultural Bank of China (601288.SS) and Industrial and Commercial Bank of China (601398.SS) , two of the country's largest state banks, said they planned to raise up to 160 billion yuan and 100 billion yuan respectively through private A-share placements to the finance ministry, China National Tobacco Corp and its subsidiaries. Both lenders said the proceeds would be used entirely to replenish core Tier 1 capital, in a move to help sustain credit expansion as Beijing leans on state banks to support growth. [USN:L4N443089 TEXT:"Weak loan demand"] remains a persistent drag on the world's second-largest economy, which also has been eroding profitability of the banking sector. The Export-Import Bank of China, one of the country's three policy lenders, said the finance ministry will inject 30 billion yuan into the bank, effectively enhancing its capital base. ($1 = 6.7108 Chinese yuan renminbi) (This story has been corrected to clarify that the ministry will lead the capital injections, not that it is committing the full amount, in the first bullet point and paragraph 1.)

item.title: Quatre morts dans des frappes israéliennes au Sud-Liban
item.description: Quatre personnes, dont deux femmes, ont été tuées dimanche dans des frappes de l'armée israélienne dans le sud du Liban, a annoncé le ministère libanais de la Santé.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Quatre personnes, dont deux femmes, ont été tuées dimanche dans des frappes de l'armée israélienne dans le sud du Liban, a annoncé le ministère libanais de la Santé. L'armée israélienne a présenté ces frappes comme des représailles à des attaques de drones du Hezbollah dans des secteurs qu'elle occupe dans le Sud-Liban. Malgré un cessez-le-feu annoncé en juin sous la médiation des Etats-Unis, l'armée israélienne reste déployée dans ce qu'elle considère comme une zone de sécurité dans le sud du Liban. Le ministère libanais de la Santé a déclaré que deux hommes avaient été tués dans une localité située à la lisière de cette zone occupée par les forces israéliennes et que deux femmes avaient aussi péri à Arab Salim, qui se trouve bien plus au nord de cette zone. L'armée israélienne avait auparavant émis un ordre d'évacuation couvrant des secteurs proches d'un immeuble à Arab Salim, qu'elle entendait bombarder en raison de son utilisation par le Hezbollah, selon elle. Deux fillettes figurent parmi les six personnes blessées dans cette frappe. Le président libanais Joseph Aoun, cité par ses services, a qualifié ces bombardements, qui ont selon lui détruit un hôpital et endommagé un bâtiment du ministère des Finances, de "dangereuse escalade" qui "révèle une stratégie d'attaques persistante qui s'étend au-delà des cibles militaires présumées pour viser des administrations et des centres de santé purement civils, reflétant une volonté manifeste de perturber le fonctionnement des institutions libanaises et de paralyser la vie quotidienne de la population". "Le président Aoun a tenu Israël pleinement responsable de cette escalade et a appelé les États-Unis et la communauté internationale à agir immédiatement pour mettre fin à ces violations et demander des comptes à ceux qui les commettent." L'armée israélienne a déclaré pour sa part avoir visé des sites de stockage d'armes du Hezbollah et un centre de commandement du mouvement chiite dans un bâtiment qui était auparavant un hôpital. Elle a affirmé avoir utilisé des armes de précision et des moyens de surveillance aérienne afin de limiter les victimes civiles. Le Hezbollah rejette les négociations directes engagées par l'Etat libanais avec Israël sous la médiation des Etats-Unis.

item.title: OPEC+ keeps oil output policy unchanged for October
item.description: OPEC+ kept its oil output policy unchanged for October at a meeting on Sunday, it said in a statement, as the producer group needs to agree new quotas before deciding its next output steps.
item.dc:creator: Ahmad Ghaddar, Olesya Astakhova, Alex Lawler
item.content:encoded: OPEC+ kept its oil output policy unchanged for October at a meeting on Sunday, it said in a statement, as the producer group needs to agree new quotas before deciding its next output steps. The meeting of seven core OPEC+ members — Saudi Arabia, Russia, Iraq, Kuwait, Algeria, Kazakhstan and Oman — comes as the Iran war continues to disrupt oil exports through the Strait of Hormuz, limiting [USN:L6N44D030 TEXT:"OPEC+'s influence"] over prices and market share. In August, OPEC+ agreed its production boost for September, completing a phased rollback of a 1.65 million-barrel-per-day supply cut first agreed in 2023. Despite the agreed production increases, the group made up of the Organization of the Petroleum Exporting Countries and its allies, including Russia, still produces far below its targets because of the war. OPEC'S POWER LIMITED BY IRAN CONFLICT "OPEC+ currently has very limited power over the physical oil market," said Jorge Leon of Rystad Energy. "The group can change production targets on paper, but it cannot guarantee that those barrels will be produced or actually reach the market." "The focus now shifts away from monthly production adjustments and towards the much more consequential debate over 2027." OPEC+ still has another layer of production cuts in place, covering most members of the 21-country group until the end of 2026. Before the group decides how to unwind the cuts and return production to the market, it needs to review members' oil production capacity to set 2027 output baselines, which form the basis for quotas. This debate will likely happen later in 2026 and hence OPEC+ is likely to [USN:L6N43U0TI TEXT:"pause its output increases"] for the fourth quarter, sources earlier told Reuters. The statement on Sunday made no mention of policy beyond October. Only the seven OPEC+ members who met on Sunday, plus the United Arab Emirates until it left OPEC in May, have been involved in monthly output decisions in recent years. The seven countries will hold their next meeting on October 4.

item.title: At flood-destroyed border, China teams scour ruins of once-busy port
item.description: The border gate was 65 feet tall. It no longer exists.
item.dc:creator: Nicoco Chan, Tingshu Wang
item.content:encoded: Chinese officials said on Sunday that workers had recovered 12 more bodies as the search continued for hundreds still missing after a tsunami-like mudslide destroyed China's main border crossing with Nepal. Rescue workers in bright orange uniforms used excavators, shovels and ground-penetrating radar to scour the now-buried site of the Gyirong border crossing. The border crossing became a grisly emblem of the devastation that followed the [USN:L1N44O06X TEXT:"collapse of a glacier"] on the Nepal side of the border on August 26 after videos showed a black wave of water, mud and debris sweeping over it with little warning. Reuters and other news agencies visited the land port, which sits in a narrow river gorge, in the first trip organised for international media by China's foreign ministry on Sunday. The mudslide has killed more than 1,300 people on both sides of the border, with more than 5,000 missing. On the Chinese side, 43 were confirmed dead and 519 remained missing as of Saturday. Among those still unaccounted for were 261 foreigners from 23 countries, officials said. There was no trace of the five-storey Chinese customs building that had stood at the border before the disaster. The only structure still visible was part of a nearby water tower installation in a barren grey-black mud field. Workers had planted a Chinese flag where the nearly 20-metre-tall border gate once stood. Behind signs warning "Danger Area Pass Quickly", groups of rescue and recovery workers dug through the debris while red excavators stood nearby. FINGERPRINTS AND TATTOOS Officials told visiting reporters that recovery teams were taking fingerprints and recording identifying features such as tattoos as bodies were recovered. They had also collected 993 personal items from the site. Families and diplomats representing countries with missing nationals have privately expressed growing frustration over what they describe as limited information-sharing by China. Beijing has not detailed how it plans to proceed with DNA identification of victims as remains are recovered, representatives of four governments told Reuters. Diplomats also said China had not answered questions about whether video from the border crossing, including facial-recognition footage, could be shared with families or used to help identify the dead. China's foreign ministry has said its release of information about the floods was "transparent and timely" and that it is ready to work with other countries and agencies. HINDU PILGRIMAGE SITE Once a historic trading hub, Gyirong had become the main crossing for trade and travellers between Nepal and Tibet after a 2015 earthquake damaged an alternative route farther east. China will consider whether it should be built back differently in the wake of the disaster, officials said. The crossing was closed between July last year and January after an earlier glacial flood. Alongside serving as a gateway for Chinese exports, including electric vehicles, it had become a transit point for Hindu pilgrims travelling through Nepal to Mount Kailash in Tibet, a sacred site for both Hindus and Buddhists. Hindus believe it to be the eternal home of Lord Shiva and his wife Parvati. Many of the foreign nationals still missing in Tibet were pilgrims with extended families in India, diplomats in Beijing have said. There are 49 Indian citizens among the missing. China has pushed back against any suggestion that it could have provided any further early warning data before the glacier collapse in Nepal. Chinese scientists have found more than 3,000 glacial lakes, of which 187 are classified as high-risk and are monitored via remote sensors or on the ground, officials told reporters. "This disaster occurred on the Nepalese side of the border, further international cooperation is required to enhance monitoring and early-warning capabilities," Norbu Tsering, deputy head of the emergency rescue headquarters, said.

JOHANNESBURG, Sept 6 : New Zealand will have to do without another of their starters for next weekend’s final match against South Africa after Luke Jacobson was added to the injury list following Saturday’s defeat in the third test. Jacobson has an elbow injury and joins captain Ardie Savea and centre Quinn Tupaea, who will miss out on the trip to Baltimore in the United States for the last international of the All Blacks' South Africa tour. It will be played next Saturday. Savea dislocated a shoulder in the first half of Saturday’s 29-24 defeat to the Springboks at Soccer City in a major blow to Kiwi hopes while centre Tupaea sustained a knee ligament tear, All Blacks officials said. South Africa, who lead the series 2-1, head to the U.S. without star winger Cheslin Kolbe, who broke his jaw in Saturday’s clash.
